name: Lyu Dalong
current_role: Non-executive director, OmniVision Integrated Circuits Group (formerly Will Semiconductor, 603501.SH); founding partner & co-chairman, Qingkong Yinxing (TusHoldings Ginkgo) venture capital
profile: Born 1962, a 1978-entry Tsinghua thermal-engineering graduate who worked as an Air Force engineering-design engineer (1983-92) before turning to investment. Through Beijing Huaqing vehicles (incl. Beijing Huaqing OmniVision Technology) he backed Will Semi's 2019 acquisition of OmniVision image sensors; he runs Tsinghua-linked VC firms Qingkong Yinxing and Ginkgo Angel Investment Center.
interesting_fact: Nominated in May 2025 to the board of Will Semi as it renamed itself OmniVision Group - one of China's largest CMOS image-sensor designers, supplying smartphone and automotive cameras.
deep_cut_fact: Tsinghua named a building after him: the 'Lyu Dalong Building' (southeast building of the Ziqiang S&T complex), a gift he and his wife He Shan made for Tsinghua's 110th anniversary, opened on 8 April 2024. He also funds young humanities faculty (2025) and an alumni lifelong-learning program.
notes: Low public profile; best known in Tsinghua alumni/VC circles. Route via OmniVision board office (board secretary Ren Bing, tel +86 21 50805043) or Qingkong Yinxing. 2025 filing says he held no shares directly - stake is indirect via Huaqing entities.

name: Binaben Nimish Chudgar
current_role: Chudgar family shareholder in Intas Pharmaceuticals (Ahmedabad); no public executive role found
profile: Listed by Hurun India (2018-2019) as a wealth holder through Intas Pharmaceuticals, the Ahmedabad generics and biosimilars maker founded by Hasmukh Chudgar and run by his sons Binish, Nimish and Urmish. The name format indicates she is linked to Nimish Chudgar (Intas joint MD), but no public source describing her could be found.
interesting_fact: Intas, the family's company, is one of India's largest privately held drugmakers and owns UK/EU generics arm Accord Healthcare.
notes: Very private; no profile, interviews or roles found under 'Binaben'/'Bina' Chudgar. Relationship to Nimish Chudgar inferred only from name format - unverified. Only route is Intas corporate office (general queries).

name: Liu Peiying
current_role: No public role found; listed by Hurun China (2010-2014) jointly with China Dongxiang chairman Chen Yihong
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2010-2014 as a co-holder (with Chen Yihong) of the fortune derived from China Dongxiang (3818.HK), the Beijing sportswear group that holds the Kappa brand in mainland China and Macau. Her exact relationship to Chen Yihong is not confirmed in any source found, and she does not appear in recent HKEX disclosure-of-interest filings.
interesting_fact: China Dongxiang owns all rights to the Italian Kappa brand in mainland China, and in 2008 bought Japan's Phenix Co., which managed Kappa and Phenix in Japan, to push into ski and outdoor fashion.
notes: No public profile; 2026 HKEX circular names the Chen family group (Chen Yihong, daughter Chen Chen, her spouse, brother Chen Yiyong) but not Liu Peiying. Likely a family member of Chen Yihong (unconfirmed). Only route is China Dongxiang IR. Off Hurun list since 2014.

name: Lyu Gang
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Zhejiang Jingxin Pharmaceutical (002020.SZ; Hong Kong H-share listing filed Sept 2026)
profile: Born 1962, Lyu Gang has run Zhejiang Jingxin Pharmaceutical, a Xinchang-born drugmaker now based in Hangzhou, since its days as Zhejiang Xinchang Jingxin Pharma; he has been chairman since 2004 when it listed in Shenzhen. With his wife he controls ~36% of the company, which focuses on CNS and cardio/cerebrovascular drugs (2025 revenue RMB4.07bn) and is seeking a second listing in Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: Jingxin's only approved innovative drug is the insomnia treatment dimdazenil (Jingnuoning); it is also developing JX2201 for elevated lipoprotein(a), and is pursuing an HKEX dual listing with CITIC Securities as sole sponsor.
deep_cut_fact: His formal education started with a mechanical-engineering associate degree from Zhejiang Radio & TV University (1987); he later did Peking University Guanghua's EMBA (2000) and a China Pharmaceutical University pharmacy certificate (2004), and earned senior-economist title in Dec 2022.
notes: Board secretary Hong Yunfei (tel 0571-86575888) is the published IR route. Company is mid-way through a Hong Kong IPO (refiled Sept 2026), so may be in a quiet period.

name: Scott D. Ferguson
current_role: Founder, Managing Partner & Portfolio Manager, Sachem Head Capital Management (NYC activist hedge fund); director, Performance Food Group; Delivery Hero supervisory board
profile: Activist investor who founded Sachem Head in 2012 after nine years at Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, which he joined at its 2003 inception. Sachem Head runs concentrated value/activist campaigns (past boards: Autodesk, Olin, Elanco, US Foods). He joined PFG's board in Sept 2025 under a cooperation deal while pushing a US Foods combination; a Sachem Head partner sits on Six Flags' board.
interesting_fact: Before investing he was a McKinsey business analyst (1996-99) and VP at private-equity firm American Industrial Partners (1999-2001); he holds a Stanford A.B. in Public Policy and a 2003 Harvard MBA.
deep_cut_fact: He was at Pershing Square from day one (2003) - joining Ackman straight out of Harvard Business School - and outside finance serves on the boards of Henry Street Settlement and the Robin Hood Foundation.

public_contacts.value: Longacre Square Partners (Dan Zacchei / Joe Germani) - Sachem@Longacresquare.com

notes: SEC 'director' flag for Six Flags (FUN) likely reflects Sachem Head's board designee Jonathan Brudnick (appointed Oct 2025), not Ferguson personally. Twilio stake is from Sachem Head's fund. Longacre Square is the best media route.

name: Zhang Weiming
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Shengjian Technology (603324.SH; formerly Shengjian Environment, renamed Aug 2024)
profile: Co-founder (with Wang Zhe) and chairman of Shanghai-based Shengjian, which supplies process-exhaust-gas treatment systems to China's semiconductor and display fabs. It grew from making a single exhaust-duct product into a full system integrator, listed on the SSE main board in April 2021, and is now pushing upstream into semiconductor equipment and materials.
interesting_fact: Shengjian dominated the niche of fab exhaust ductwork before 2011, then rode BOE-led domestic display-panel build-outs into full waste-gas treatment systems; Zhang's motto is to 'take the hardest road' and build a 'hundred-year company'.
deep_cut_fact: In its start-up years Shengjian's stainless-steel coated exhaust duct won FM Approvals certification for cleanroom exhaust/smoke duct systems; Zhang compares the climb upmarket to mountaineering: 'the higher you go, the fewer companions, the more beautiful the view.'
notes: Re-elected chairman 2024. Highly relevant to semiconductor-fab infrastructure angle. IR route is the board office.
